newsitem.title: USA: Ferro says exchange rates hurt sales.
newsitem.headline: Ferro says exchange rates hurt sales.

text.p: Ferro Corp said Monday its first quarter sales were hurt by currency exchange rates.

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Albert Bersticker said, "We are very pleased with our improved earnings. This was accomplished at a time when exchange rates in Europe worked very much against us."
Net income was $15.2 million, up 16 percent from a year earlier.

Excluding the currency effect, sales from ongoing operations would have shown an improvement of four percent over the first quarter of 1996. Actual sales were $342.2 million, down two percent from $348.2 million a year earlier.
Bersticker said that "if such gains could have been reported in operating income, operating margins would have been even better."
The company had a strategy to hedge against currency movements, which produced gains which were recorded below operating income and which offset the unfavorable effects of exchange rates.
Ferro is a producer of industrial specialty materials, including coatings, colors, ceramics, chemicals and plastics.
